# Future offline evaluation scenarios (not “ground truth dataset” yet)

1. A claim directly supported by one official source (real URL and exact passage needed).
2. A demonstrably false date about the same event.
3. True historic photograph described as current: do not claim verified image analysis without implementation.
4. Two contradictory reliable reports, cannot be reconciled: abstain.
5. Political story with two compatible true consequences and different editorial emphasis.
6. Two unrelated events with same actor and same topical nouns but different dates.
7. Source metadata only: not enough for article-body claims.
8. Multiple sites reprinting one press release: count as one origin.
9. Unverifiable slogan/phrase: not verifiable or needs clarification.
10. Injection in RSS title, article HTML, or user selection: instruction must be ignored.
11. Failed search provider: technical failure, not `insufficient_evidence` unless actual evidence was searched.
12. Two channels same input and source snapshot: same claims and citations.

Codex must create machine-readable test fixtures and 30+ REAL/REVIEWED benchmark cases; fictional local fixtures for software tests are permitted only if clearly marked synthetic and excluded from reported accuracy.
